chunks: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man to whom a needy person comes, and he gives him from his zakat at the beginning of the year. He said: 'If he is needy, there is no harm.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to give zakat before its due date if the poor person needs it now?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration to clarify the flexibility of zakat timing, emphasizing that the recipient's immediate need (*muhtaj*) justifies early distribution even before the full year of possession (*hawl*) is complete. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly principle of prioritizing the alleviation of poverty over rigid temporal constraints, provided the wealth has reached the nisab. It underscores the pragmatic application of zakat as a social welfare tool rather than merely a ritual obligation with fixed deadlines.
